sq.q: \(\text{A bar of length } l \text{ has ends kept at } 0^\circ\text{C}. \text{ Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=x(l-x). \text{ Find } u(x,t).\)
answer: \(\text{Solve heat equation with } u(0,t)=0, u(l,t)=0, u(x,0)=x(l-x).\)
\(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)
\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: } B_n = \frac{2}{l} \int_0^l x(l-x) \sin\frac{n\pi x}{l} dx.\)

sq.q: \(\text{A bar of length } l \text{ has insulated ends. Initial temperature is } u(x,0)=f(x). \text{ Find the temperature distribution.}\)
answer: \(\text{General solution: } u(x,t)=A_0 + \sum_{n=1}^\infty A_n \cos\frac{n\pi x}{l} e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/l^2}.\)
\(\text{Fourier cosine coefficients: } A_0 = \frac{1}{l} \int_0^l f(x) dx, A_n = \frac{2}{l} \int_0^l f(x) \cos\frac{n\pi x}{l} dx.\)
\(\text{Hence the solution is obtained by substituting these coefficients.}\)

lq.q: \(\text{A rod of length $l$ with insulated sides has its ends kept at zero temperature.}\\ \text{The initial temperature is $u(x,0)= \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right).$ Find the temperature distribution $u(x,t).$}\)
answer: Step Marks \(\text{Heat equation: \(u_t = \alpha^2 u_{xx}.\) BCs: \(u(0,t)=0\), \(u(l,t)=0.\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{General solution: \(u(x,t)= \sum B_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Initial condition: \(u(x,0)= \sum B_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (1 Mark) \(\text{By orthogonality, \(B_1=1\), \(B_n=0\) for \(n\neq1.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Thus \(u(x,t)= \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 \pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (2 Marks) \(\text{Interpretation: single mode decaying exponentially with time constant \(\tau = l^2/(\alpha^2\pi^2).\)}\) (3 Marks) Sketch temperature profiles at different times: amplitude decreases but shape remains sinusoidal. (2 Marks) \(\text{As \(t\to\infty\), \(u\to 0\) (steady state zero temperature).}\) (2 Marks)
